prompt:
Create a complete 1440 × 900 desktop web portfolio homepage for John Paul Fernandez, edge to edge with no browser frame. It helps potential clients and collaborators understand his actual profile and technology range. Use the real portrait reference and preserve John’s identity.

This is a clearly different composition within The Cutaway Folio world. Keep cobalt, coral-red, acid-yellow, chalk, graphite, precise construction marks, bold editorial typography, and layered cut-color planes. Give the page an asymmetrical editorial structure: a tall chalk profile column occupies the left third, with name, role, real paragraph, and “See my work”; on the right two-thirds, a single large circular/elliptical cutaway diagram uses the portrait as its center and three clearly separated orbital bands for Interfaces, Applications, and Backend systems. Arrange the real technologies along those bands as crisp readable labels. The diagram must feel like a technical section drawing made from flat graphic planes, not a dashboard, not app screenshots, and not literal architecture. Keep the header compact across the top. Begin Selected projects along the lower edge on an uninterrupted chalk plane. This radial composition must not resemble a portrait centered between left-side copy and right-side stacked zones, nor a horizontal strip of three skill panels.

Use exactly “John Paul Fernandez”, “Full Stack Developer”, “Fast, clear, dependable web products”, “I like building web products that feel fast, clear, and dependable. Most of my work lives at the intersection of React interfaces, Next.js apps, and backend systems that are simple to scale and maintain.”, “3+ years building web products”, “Interfaces”, “Applications”, “Backend systems”. Include only React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Docker, Git, Firebase, and Nginx. Include navigation About, Work, Experience, Contact, and “Project writeups are not published yet”. Do not invent projects, labels, metrics, employers, clients, or testimonials.
